content.title: About
content.content: Boneless, skinless chicken thigh is a lean cut taken from the thigh portion after removing the bone and skin. It is raw, light pink, with a tender texture and a mild poultry aroma. This cut is commonly used for sautéing, grilling, roasting, and braising.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken thighs contain more iron than chicken breast.
Without bone and skin they cook faster and more evenly.
In many countries they are called “thigh fillet”, “boneless thigh” or “skinless thigh”.
Raw chicken must be kept at 4 °C or below to prevent bacterial growth.
Thigh meat absorbs marinades better than breast meat.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 helps with amino‑acid metabolism and supports the nervous system.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is essential for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Chicken thigh is virtually carbohydrate‑free, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Provides selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports thyroid health.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: High sodium in processed versions
items.content: Pre‑marinated thighs can contain a lot of added salt.

items.title: Spoilage if improperly stored
items.content: Storing above 4 °C leads to rapid spoilage and off‑odors.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boneless, skinless thighs can be pan‑fried, baked, grilled, or cooked in a slow cooker. Marinating in olive oil, herbs, spices, and lemon juice before cooking enhances flavor. Cook until juices run clear and the internal temperature reaches 74 °C.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw thighs in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑grade bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw frozen thighs in the fridge before use.
